From: Alex Chan <alex@cloudfolio.com>

Subject: Optimize toolkit pricing and technical fit

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Cloudfolio is evaluating Redwood for a multi‑model assistant we plan to ship H1 2027. A few things we'd like clarity on before we proceed to procurement:

- Pricing: rough guidance for a pilot (3 months) vs an initial production commit (12 months) assuming ~120M tokens/month generation + 30M embedding tokens/month.
- Optimize toolkit: how packaging works — is this an add‑on per‑model, per‑project, or per‑account? Any lift in unit economics we should expect from KV caching + batching?
- Quantization: we run a mix of latency‑sensitive (chat) and batch (offline summarization) workloads. Can you outline recommended quant profiles (int8, int4/FP4) and any caveats about hallucination/regression risk?
- Requirements: we're sensitive to 99th percentile latency (target < 250ms for chat at 95% of requests). We'd also like to test at 500 QPS sustained during a pilot.

Can you put together a short scenario that maps configuration -> expected token cost delta and risk notes? Procurement will want that for the SOW.

Thanks,
Alex Chan
Head of ML — Cloudfolio

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a short pricing scenarios PDF that maps config -> expected unit economics. Karthik and Marcus are looped in for the technical / ops constraints.

Pilot vs Commit (hightlights):
- Pilot (3 months): Optimize toolkit available as an add‑on SKU during the pilot. Typical pilot package we recommend: 100k credits (applied to tokens), Optimize add‑on at a blended $X/month credit consumption (see attached). Pilot includes access to KV caching and batching config presets.
- Production commit (12 months): Commit pricing replaces credits with a monthly committed throughput band. With a committed band sized to your 120M gen tokens/mo we can offer tiered discounts (example: 12% off hosted list + 1x month free for first quarter).

Optimize packaging:
- Add‑on model: Optimize toolkit is an account-level add‑on that provides per‑model configuration profiles (caching, batching, quant recommendations). If you want model‑specific SLAs/variants, we surface that as per‑model bundles for Dedicated deployments.
- Economics: KV prefix caching yields the largest near‑term token savings for chat (20–45% depending on repetition and prompt structure). Batching reduces per token GPU time for high concurrency workloads, but benefits are workload dependent (10–30%). Quantization can reduce model compute cost by ~1.3–3x depending on profile and hardware.

Quantization guidance (summary):
- Latency‑sensitive chat: start with int8 (safe, low regression risk). On identical hardware int8 typically preserves generation quality and gives ~1.3× speedup.
- Aggressive cost reduction: int4/FP4 can be used for batch summarization and retrieval‑augmented generation where outputs are post‑processed/validated. Expect larger efficiency gains (2–3×) but run evals on critical prompts.
- On Dedicated: we support int4 inference paths with constrained model families; we'll validate with a short quantization evaluation. For Hosted, int8 is the baseline we recommend initially.

Latency SLOs and 500 QPS pilot:
- With KV prefix caching and a batching policy tuned for chat (small microbatches, prioritize latency), hitting 99p < 250ms is feasible for single‑request sizes under ~1k tokens on dedicated capacity. Hosted can achieve similar at lower QPS; for 500 sustained QPS we recommend a temporary Dedicated pool during the pilot.

Next steps:
1) Marcus can put together a pilot SOW + ops checklist (I'll attach a draft).
2) If you agree, we'll run a short quantization eval on a representative prompt set (we can seed with 200 prompts).
3) We can propose two pricing lines in the SOW: Pilot credits bundle + optional Dedicated staging for load testing.

I'm attaching "optimize-pricing-scenarios.pdf" which contains three scenarios and delta math. Would you like us to prepare a short 30–45m technical call this week?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

Ben / Alex — quick follow up with the concrete items procurement asked for. Karthik drafted the quant table and Marcus pulled pilot ops numbers below. I've attached a short SOW draft (pilot-sow-draft.docx).

Quantization quick table (Karthik):
- int8 (recommended for chat):
  - Latency: ~1.25× faster than FP16 on our runtime (measured on A100-class nodes for Llama2 family)
  - Compute multiplier: ~0.75× cost of FP16
  - Quality/regression note: minimal; run anchor prompts but low risk for mild hallucination changes

- int4 (cost‑first, batch workloads):
  - Latency: ~1.8–2.5× faster than FP16 depending on kernel and sequence length
  - Compute multiplier: ~0.4–0.6× cost of FP16
  - Quality/regression note: moderate risk; recommend A/B evals and thresholding for critical prompts

Pilot ops cost (Marcus):
- Temporary Dedicated pool sized for 500 sustained QPS (chat profile, median request 250 tokens): estimate $X/month (line item in SOW). Hosted bursting option: workable for short soak tests but carries unpredictable egress/backoff risk at sustained 500 QPS; we recommend Dedicated for predictable latency and a clean test.

Credits portability:
- We can make unused pilot credits convertible to commit value for a 12‑month purchase (subject to standard terms): any unused credits (up to 50% of pilot purchase) can be applied as a one‑time credit against the first invoice of the commit term. We'll include that clause in the SOW draft.

Commercial concession (proposal):
- Pilot package: 100k credits + Optimize add‑on (trial rate) + Dedicated staging for 1 month for load testing.
- If you convert to a 12‑month commit within 30 days of pilot completion: 10% off the first 3 months of committed invoice and allocation of unused pilot credits per the portability clause above.

Attachments: pilot‑sow‑draft.docx (SOW + line items), and the earlier pricing PDF.

Next steps:
- Confirm call Thursday 11am PT and we'll bring solutions + infra.
- Share a 200‑prompt sample set for quantization eval (we'll sign an NDA addendum if prompts contain PII).

Open to adjustments.

Thanks,
